name: Plastics Plus
old_description: Since 1998, we have specialized in custom plastic fabrication, along with offering a large variety of standard sized acrylic sign holders, and a variety of other standard products. If you do not find a style or a size that will satisfy your needs already on our website, we would be happy to work with you to create a custom design. Custom design options are available to you on all of our products including ballot boxes, donation boxes, business card holders, and risers, and custom designs do not have to be expensive. We will work to find the most cost effective way to meet your display needs, and our estimates are always free.
about:
Plastics Plus operates from Bismarck, North Dakota, where it was founded in January 1998 by a hobby woodworker who needed a small piece of Plexiglas for a project. The company has since grown into a manufacturer of custom plastic fabrications and standard acrylic displays, selling across the United States and Canada.

Its Bismarck facility handles orders ranging from a few pieces to several thousand units, with cut‑to‑size sheet stock also available.

Plastics Plus serves businesses, organizations, and individuals in healthcare (hospitals and clinics use chart holders and bio card holders), retail and marketing (point‑of‑purchase signage, trade‑show displays), funeral homes, construction (window well covers), and safety (glove box holders). Government and civic customers purchase ballot boxes, while distributors benefit from blind‑shipping and multi‑location fulfillment.

The founder’s original need for a single plastic piece shaped a culture of no minimum orders, no broken‑case fees, and free estimates on custom work. The company emphasizes made‑in‑America production — virtually all items are fabricated in‑house — along with fast turnaround times and personal customer service as its primary differentiators.

name: Plastipak Packaging Inc
old_description: One of those innovations was the creation of Plastipak—founded in 1967 to solve the problem of the heavy five-gallon jugs used to deliver water. With a full load of water in them, these five-gallon jugs weighed 50 pounds and required superior strength to manage. Plastic seemed the ideal solution to lighten the load, as did manufacturing the plastic in-house. The success of the lightened bottle was the start of Plastipak’s ongoing innovation and success.
about:
Plastipak Packaging Inc. was founded in 1967 in Champaign, Illinois, by Bill Young, who joined his family's water delivery business after graduating from the University of Detroit. The company began as an in-house solution to the heavy five-gallon glass jugs used for water delivery, replacing them with lighter, stronger plastic containers manufactured on site. The Young family has retained ownership through successive generations, embedding a heritage of hands-on innovation into the company's culture.

Today Plastipak operates as a global manufacturer of rigid plastic packaging and recycling solutions, with more than 50 production sites across North America, South America, Europe, Africa, and Asia. Its core processes include extrusion blow molding, injection stretch blow molding (ISBM), PET and ePET molding, wide-mouth container technology, hot-fill and barrier container engineering, decoration (embossing, debossing, direct-object printing), and the production of both virgin and post-consumer recycled (PCR) resins. The company holds over 500 U.S. patents and more than 1,000 international patents, reflecting a portfolio of proprietary systems such as the rotary dual-cavity ISBM machine, the 30-station G.E.M. PAK extrusion wheel, and recent innovations like SprayPET Revolution™ aerosol packaging, PPK Natura™ carbon-waste PET resin, and O2blox™ nylon-free oxygen barrier.

Plastipak serves a broad range of end markets, including carbonated and non-carbonated beverages, hot-fill juices and teas, beer, UHT milk, dairy, household and commercial products (detergents, personal care), automotive, industrial, and agricultural chemicals. Long-standing customers have included Pepsi, Kraft, Heineken, Downy Unstopables, and Hilltop Honey, illustrating the company's reach across multinational brands and regional producers alike.

The business was created to solve a specific logistics problem—reducing the weight and breakage of water delivery jugs—and that problem-solving mindset remains central. Plastipak differentiates itself through vertical integration (in-house resin production, mold design, recycling via its Clean Tech centers), a global footprint that enables local service, and a sustained investment in circular-economy technologies that turn post-consumer waste into new packaging.

name: Podiumwear Custom Sports Apparel
old_description: Since 2003, Podiumwear has redefined what it means to create custom uniforms—making the process fun, effortless, and stress-free. Our mission? To ensure that every design feels like a superhero suit, empowering athletes to conquer the trails, pitch, track, or road with confidence and pride.
about:
Podiumwear Custom Sports Apparel was founded in 2003 in St. Paul, Minnesota, by Reid Lutter, a nordic ski racer and coach with four decades of trail experience. Frustrated by the difficulties of ordering custom uniforms for his own teams, Lutter set out to build a company that would make the process enjoyable and stress‑free, starting with nordic ski apparel before expanding into cycling, running, and soccer.

The company produces fully custom team uniforms and apparel — jerseys, tops, shorts, training jackets, pants, and socks — for a wide range of sports including cycling, nordic skiing, running, soccer, volleyball, football, basketball, hockey, lacrosse, clay target sports, softball, baseball, mountain biking, cross‑country, and track and field. Customers work one‑on‑one with designers or use an online customizer, and orders can be shipped directly to each athlete or to a single team contact. A partnership with The North Face and U.S. Ski & Snowboard adds a high‑profile dimension to its nordic program.

Podiumwear serves youth, club, and school teams across the United States and internationally. Its customers include team uniform directors, coaches, administrators, and parents who need reliable, on‑time delivery for seasonal competition. The company highlights testimonials from a team uniform director, a team administrator, and a club parent, underscoring its focus on easing the administrative burden of uniform procurement.

Lutter’s original goal — concierge‑level service, fast turnaround, and top‑tier quality — remains the stated differentiator. Podiumwear emphasizes total design freedom without templates, durability that lasts multiple seasons, and a policy that allows two below‑minimum re‑orders per calendar year to accommodate roster changes.

name: Point Medical Corporation
old_description: Point Medical specializes in the custom development and fabrication of implant grade silicone rubber devices and assemblies that meet the exacting tolerances and specifications required for the medical environment.
about:
Point Medical Corporation operates from Crown Point, Indiana, where it develops and fabricates implant-grade silicone rubber devices and assemblies for medical applications. The company focuses on custom development and fabrication to meet exacting tolerances and specifications required in the medical environment.

The facility is FDA-registered and ISO 13485:2016 certified, with a Class 10,000 clean room. In-house prototype development and tooling accelerate the transition to production. Capabilities span extrusion (custom, multi-lumen, co-extrusion, miniature profiles, wire-reinforced, striped, close-tolerance, translucent, radiopaque), catheter assembly (smooth transition tube-to-lumen molding, balloons, coil forming, printing, complete fabrication, latex-to-silicone conversion), molding (liquid injection, top transfer, compression, insert), and tipping (forming, clean-cut holes, step cutting, taper and bullet tips).

Point Medical serves medical device manufacturers and clinical consultants, providing custom silicone rubber components for applications such as catheters, tubing, and implantable assemblies. The company also operates Martech Medical Products for non-silicone plastics manufacturing.

The company emphasizes an ongoing inquiry into the latest technology, materials, and manufacturing methods to ensure custom product performance. Its reputation for quality and innovative design stems from consistent attention to materials, machining, and manufacturing techniques.

name: Port Erie Plastics
old_description: Founded in Harborcreek, Pennsylvania, in 1953, Port Erie Plastics remains family-owned and engineering-driven. We combine the responsiveness of a privately held manufacturer with the infrastructure of a large-scale production partner.
about:
Port Erie Plastics was founded in 1953 in Harborcreek, Pennsylvania, and remains a family-owned, engineering-driven manufacturer. The company began as a plastics processor and has grown into a large-scale production partner while retaining the responsiveness of a privately held business.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding and structural foam injection molding for large components, with wall thicknesses from 0.200 to 0.500 inches and part lengths up to 7.5 feet. Its facility runs nearly 90 injection molding machines in a 24/7 production environment, supported by a full-service in-house tool room that handles mold building, refurbishment, and maintenance. Port Erie also manages structured tool transfers and validation, often bringing transferred molds into steady production within days.

Port Erie serves OEMs across consumer products, office furniture, durable goods, building materials, home improvement, kitchen and appliance components, electronic housings, material handling, lawn and garden, and building and construction. Past programs include structural foam redesign of HDPE trench drains for the construction industry, injection molding of polypropylene and elastomer lids for cookware, and development of combination dials for safe manufacturing. The company also supported an urgent medical product mold transfer that restored production in a single weekend.

The company says its differentiation lies in disciplined tooling control, process validation, and a project engineer assigned to each program for technical ownership from quote through full production. Its core values—Protect, Engage, Perform—guide a focus on long-term partnerships, supply continuity, and protection of customer tooling investments.

name: Poward Plastics Inc
old_description: Poward Plastics is a leading American manufacturer of high-quality plastic injection molded products and services. Whatever your specific job demands, you can count on Poward Plastics for thermoplastic injected and precision insert molded products, whether your industry is food and beverage, medical, automotive, packaging/displays, or any other field that utilizes plastics in its manufacturing.
about:
Based in Reading, Pennsylvania, Poward Plastics has been producing custom plastic injection molded parts for over 50 years. The company is family-owned and operated across multiple generations, with materials sourced from U.S. suppliers and all manufacturing completed domestically.

The shop runs injection molding presses from 25 to 120 tons in-house and partners with facilities up to 6,000 tons, with a maximum press size of 1,400 tons. It produces parts up to 78.7 × 59 × 31.5 inches, holding tolerances of ±0.002 inch. Services include insert molding, overmolding, prototype and production tooling (aluminum and P20 steel), multi-cavity and family molds, mold building, repair, and maintenance, as well as 3D printing and CNC modeling for prototyping. Minimum orders start at 100 parts with a $5,000 threshold.

Customers span medical (valves, syringes, bushings), automotive (plugs, fittings), electronics (housings, accessories), aerospace and defense (ITAR-registered), food and beverage, packaging and displays, industrial, and government sectors. The company ships nationwide and offers free local delivery in the Reading area.

Poward Plastics emphasizes domestic sourcing and production, mold storage and warehousing for reorders, and experience transferring tooling from offshore manufacturers. It holds ITAR and RoHS certifications and provides design engineering assistance, rapid tooling in two weeks, and production tooling in three weeks.

name: Power Plus
old_description: Power Plus is a California power solutions provider focused on rental and turnkey power systems. Offers generators, temporary power switchgear and distribution (including ATS and transformers) for construction sites, industrial projects and emergency power needs. Operates 24/7.
about:
Power Plus is headquartered in Anaheim, California, and was founded in 1987 by Steve Bray. Bray, a former electrician working on Southern California construction sites, recognized that contractors needed more than equipment—they needed reliable problem-solvers. The company began as a small temporary power operation in Orange County.

Today, Power Plus operates nationwide with 500–999 employees and describes itself as the largest independent power solutions provider in America. The company runs four integrated divisions—Construction Services, Portable Power Solutions, Critical Power Solutions, and Designed Video Surveillance (DVS)—offering generator rentals, temporary power switchgear and distribution (including automatic transfer switches and transformers), backup power installations, fuel management, and U.S.-based live video monitoring. Services span utility infrastructure, permanent electrical installation, and portable equipment sales.

The company serves construction, oil and gas, mining, disaster response, agriculture, healthcare, data centers, retail distribution, commercial facilities, critical infrastructure, and telecommunications. Its customer base includes Amazon, Walmart, Costco, and roughly half of the Fortune 100. In the 1990s, Power Plus supplied power for global entertainment productions such as the Rolling Stones tour, Olympic events, and the Super Bowl.

Power Plus emphasizes a problem-solving culture: technicians walk sites, listen to requirements, and design custom solutions rather than offering cookie-cutter packages. The firm maintained a no-layoff policy during the COVID-19 pandemic, reflecting a people-first philosophy rooted in Bray’s original vision of doing whatever it takes to deliver power whenever and wherever it is needed.
